title: Smooth cohomological duality without a chosen orientation
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $N\geq1$ an integer with $NA=0$. Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible, and let $f:X\to S$ be smooth, separated, compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable], and of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Work in the entire ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring $A_T$ on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with inverse image $f^*=f^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $f^\times$ be the right adjoint of the ordinary etale compact-support functor $Rf_!$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-amb-etale-compact-support], and put $\omega_f=f^\times A_S$. Then $\omega_f[-2d]$ is isomorphic to a sheaf $L$ in degree zero which is etale locally isomorphic to $A_X$ (a locally constant sheaf of free rank-one $A$-modules). For every $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the canonical tensor morphism
$$f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\longrightarrow f^\times K$$
is an isomorphism. Here the canonical morphism is the transpose, under $Rf_!\dashv f^\times$, of the inverse compact-support projection formula followed by $1_K\otimes\epsilon_{A_S}$ and the tensor unit constraint:
$$Rf_!(f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f)\longrightarrow K\otimes_A^LRf_!\omega_f\longrightarrow K\otimes_A^LA_S\longrightarrow K.$$
This statement concerns ordinary etale coefficients, not the unbounded pro-etale category. No orientation of $L$ is chosen.

proof.text: Choose a compactification $f=rj$. For an open immersion, the extension-by-zero stalk is the original stalk in the open and zero outside. Consequently $j_!(j^*P\otimes Q)\cong P\otimes j_!Q$: at a point in the open it is the identity tensor comparison and outside both sides vanish. This holds for total complexes as well. Compute the derived tensor with a K-flat resolution with flat terms of $K$; its inverse image stays K-flat by the ringed-topos tensor-pullback lemma. Since $j_!$ is exact, the termwise comparison computes the derived one. Apply the proper projection formula for $r$ to $j_!M$ to obtain $Rf_!(f^*K\otimes^L M)\cong K\otimes^LRf_!M$, for all unbounded $K,M$. In particular set $M=\omega_f$, compose with the adjunction counit at $A_S$ and the tensor unit constraint, and transpose. This constructs the claimed global map $\alpha_{f,K}$. All schemes in the compactification are Noetherian, since $S$ is Noetherian and the morphisms are finite type.

The comparison in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] is used only with the following unbounded justification, not with its bounded-below source proof. Apply [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] to every proper rectangle, with coefficient ring $A$ (it is torsion because $NA=0$). For an open $v:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ and proper $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$, write $V=p^{-1}Y$, $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$. Form the map $v_!Rp_{Y*}M\to Rp_*b_!M$ as the adjunct for $v_!\dashv v^*$ of the inverse open proper exchange $Rp_{Y*}M\cong v^*Rp_*b_!M$. Over $Y$ this is that exchange; at a geometric point outside $Y$, unbounded proper exchange identifies the right side with the cohomology of the fibre of $b_!M$, which is zero because the fibre misses $V$. The left side is zero by extension-by-zero stalks. Exact restriction and the stalk criterion applied to each cohomology sheaf prove it is an isomorphism for every $M\in D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. For a proper refinement $a:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ extending the identity of $X$, over $X$ the open $X\hookrightarrow a^{-1}X$ is a section of the separated map $a^{-1}X\to X$, hence clopen by [lem-weil-pbc-open-section-clopen]. Extension by zero is $M$ on that component and zero on its complement, so the same argument gives $j_{2!}M\cong Ra_*j_{1!}M$, with identity on $X$ and zero fibres outside $X$.
For coherence, use the canonical derived pushforward composition of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Every exchange is the mate of the equality of inverse images: its transpose is the inverse-image comparison followed by the pulled-back counit. For two rectangles substitute the composite counit $\epsilon_{ba}=\epsilon_b\circ Rb_*(\epsilon_a)$; naturality moves the intervening pullback comparison past $\epsilon_a$, giving precisely the transpose for the outer rectangle. Thus the two exchanges agree by the adjunction bijection, for arbitrary unbounded arguments. The same calculation with three counits proves associativity, and the identity counit proves the identity law. For the open-extension maps, transpose instead under $v_!\dashv v^*$: restrictions of the two proposed composites are the just-equal pasted exchanges, so the composites agree. This proves refinement coherence without claiming that equality of derived morphisms can be tested on stalks. The Noetherian bases are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the source opens in the Noetherian compactifications are quasi-compact. Thus [prop-nagata-compactification-category], clauses (i) and (ii), supplies common proper refinements and equalizing refinements. Comparing through a common refinement gives independence of compactification; equalizing parallel refinements and the composition law just proved gives independence of the chosen maps into it. Compactify $g$ as $Y\xrightarrow{v}\overline Y\xrightarrow{r}S$ and $vf$ as $X\xrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y$; existence is Nagata. Then $X\hookrightarrow V\to Y$ compactifies $f$. Apply the proved map to $M$ equal to extension by zero from $X$ into $V$, and apply $Rr_*$. This gives the canonical $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$; the pasted-exchange identity just proved gives its associativity and refinement independence. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] makes each proper rectangle commute with its tensor projection map. The open rectangle commutes termwise with tensor by the two extension-by-zero stalk cases of step 1. Consequently the resulting composition identifies $P_{gf}$ with $P_g\circ Rg_!(P_f)$, with the usual pullback and tensor associators. These comparisons supply exactly the unbounded composition used below.

proof.text:
At each point of $X$, the smooth local normal form supplies affine opens $U\subset X$, $V\subset S$ and an etale map $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$. The dimension in this form is the given $d$: the etale map has zero-dimensional relative fibres, and [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] says that projection from affine space has relative dimension equal to its number of coordinates; apply [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] to the etale map and that projection. At the chosen point the resulting dimension equals $d$, so the chart integer is $d$. Compose the etale map with the open immersion $\mathbf A^d_V\subset\mathbf A^d_S$ to obtain a separated finite-type etale $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$ with $fu=p_de$, where $u:U\hookrightarrow X$. Thus the original base $S$ is retained. The maps $u,e,p_d,fu$ are compactifiable by Nagata, applied to their separated finite-type maps and qcqs Noetherian bases. Use the ordinary-etale projective-line adjunction [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], restrict by the exact open extension adjunction to affine lines, and iterate using step 2. This supplies $Rp_{d!}\dashv p_d^*(d)[2d]$ with its twist explicitly $A(1)=\mu_N\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A$ on the ordinary etale site. In particular it makes no identification with def-coefficient-twists-detailed. Etale adjoint locality for $u$ and $e$ then identifies
$$u^*f^\times K\cong (fu)^\times K\cong e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d],\qquad u^*\omega_f\cong A_U(d)[2d].$$
Here the finite etale twist is defined by the new ordinary projective-line input, with the same annihilator $N$ as the twist-line lemma. The affine iteration uses pullback of roots of unity and the tensor identity $A(1)^{\otimes d}=A(d)$, not an adic comparison. Step 4 below fixes the counit of that iterated adjunction. The identification is the unique comparison of right adjoints through their Hom bijections.

proof.text:
Fix the normalization of the affine-space adjunction, rather than merely an abstract isomorphism of its right adjoint. On $\mathbf P^1_S$, the adjunction counit is, by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] for our arbitrary finite $A$,
$$Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]\cong K\otimes^LRq_*A(1)[2]\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_q}K.$$
For $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$, the right adjoint of $Rq_*j_!$ is $j^*q^*(1)[2]$. Its counit is $Rq_*$ of the counit $j_!j^*\to\mathrm{id}$ followed by the displayed counit. The open-immersion tensor comparison from step 1 sends this composite to $1_K$ tensored with its value at $A_S$. Use the unbounded composition comparison proved in step 2. Iterating the affine-line factorization of $p_d$ gives the same assertion for $p_d$: the composite counit is obtained by successively applying the $d$ line counits. For $d=0$ it is the identity. Tensor reassociation sends $x\otimes m_1\otimes\cdots\otimes m_d$ to the same tensor at each stage, so its transpose is exactly the canonical isomorphism $p_d^*K\otimes^LA(d)[2d]\cong p_d^*K(d)[2d]$.

For a separated finite-type etale map $v$, its sum-extension definition gives, at each geometric point, one summand for each lift to the source. Indeed, a germ in the defining sum presheaf has finite support; each map to the etale source determines a lift of the geometric point, and equal germs of these maps agree on a common pointed etale neighbourhood. Conversely a lift is represented on such a neighbourhood. Taking the filtered colimit therefore gives exactly the sum over lifts, and exactness of geometric stalks lets this computation pass through cohomology. The sheaf tensor definition gives its stalk as the tensor of stalks: both sides are the filtered colimit of the section tensors, since every finite tensor expression and every relation occurs on a common neighbourhood. Tensoring by an inverse-image complex distributes over these sums; the comparison sends $x\otimes m$ in the summand of a lift to the same tensor in that summand. The counit $v_!v^*B\to B$ is the fold map, so this tensor comparison commutes with the counit. This can be checked on K-flat models: inverse image preserves K-flatness, $v_!$ is exact, and its total sums preserve the termwise tensor identification. Thus it also holds on the unbounded derived categories. Apply the comparison and fold-counit identity separately to the factorizations $h=fu$ and $h=p_de$. Write $F=Rf_!$, $G=f^\times$, and $P_g$ for the projection isomorphism $Rg_!(g^*K\otimes M)\to K\otimes Rg_!M$ of step 1. For $h=fu$, the canonical right-adjoint comparison gives $h^\times=u^*G$, and its counit at $B$ is
$$\epsilon_{h,B}=\epsilon_{f,B}\circ F(\epsilon_{u,GB}).$$
The transpose under $Ru_!\dashv u^*$ of $u^*\alpha_{f,K}$ is the composite
$$Ru_!(h^*K\otimes u^*\omega_f)\xrightarrow{P_u} f^*K\otimes Ru_!u^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{u,\omega_f}}f^*K\otimes\omega_f\xrightarrow{\alpha_{f,K}}GK.$$
Indeed naturality of the fold counit moves $Ru_!u^*\alpha_{f,K}$ past that counit, and the fold/tensor identity above gives the first two arrows. Applying $F$ and then $\epsilon_{f,K}$ transposes once more. The defining transpose of $\alpha_{f,K}$, naturality of $P_f$ in its second variable, and the formula for $\epsilon_h$ identify the result with $P_h$ followed by $1_K\otimes\epsilon_{h,A}$. Here the composition comparison identifies $P_h$ with first applying $F(P_u)$ and then $P_f$: both projection maps are obtained from the pullback tensor comparison and adjunction evaluation; substituting the composite evaluation applies these two evaluations in that order. Thus $u^*\alpha_{f,K}$ is the canonical tensor mate for $h$. For $h=p_de$, put $H=Rp_{d!}$ and $J=p_d^\times$. Under $Re_!\dashv e^*$ the transpose of $e^*\alpha_{p_d,K}$ is explicitly
$$Re_!(h^*K\otimes e^*A(d)[2d])\xrightarrow{P_e}p_d^*K\otimes Re_!e^*A(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{e,A(d)[2d]}}p_d^*K\otimes A(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\alpha_{p_d,K}}JK.$$
Applying $H$ and then $\epsilon_{p_d,K}$ replaces the last arrow by $P_{p_d}$ followed by $1_K\otimes\epsilon_{p_d,A}$. Naturality of $P_{p_d}$ moves $\epsilon_e$ into its second factor. Step 2 identifies the first two projection arrows with $P_h$, and the remaining arrows with $1_K\otimes\epsilon_{h,A}$. Thus this transpose is the canonical tensor mate for $h$, with counit $\epsilon_{p_d,B}\circ Rp_{d!}(\epsilon_{e,p_d^\times B})$; this is an alternative expression for the counit of $h$, not an additional counit after the $u$-counit. The unbounded compact-support composition and tensor compatibilities proved in step 2, and uniqueness of the right-adjoint Hom bijections identify the two expressions. Step 4 makes $\alpha_{p_d,K}$ the tensor reassociation isomorphism, and exact inverse image and the derived tensor-pullback comparison preserve it. Hence $u^*\alpha_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism for every chart $U$.

Inverse image on etale module sheaves is exact, so it commutes with cohomology. The charts of step 3 cover $X$, and step 5 therefore makes every geometric stalk of every cohomology map $\mathcal H^i(\alpha_{f,K})$ an isomorphism. Apply the geometric-stalk criterion to each underlying abelian cohomology sheaf. Every $\mathcal H^i(\alpha_{f,K})$ is an isomorphism; equivalently its cone is acyclic, so $\alpha_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category. This uses no bounded-below hypothesis and applies the sheaf-level criterion only to sheaves.

The local model $u^*\omega_f\cong A_U(d)[2d]$ and the twist-line lemma give $\mathcal H^i(\omega_f)=0$ for $i\ne-2d$: exact inverse image and the sheaf-stalk criterion detect this vanishing. Put $L=\mathcal H^{-2d}(\omega_f)$. It is locally isomorphic to $A_U(d)$, and refining the chart by a twist trivialization makes it isomorphic to $A$, which is precisely the stated local rank-one condition. To identify the complex globally, take a representative $C$ of $\omega_f$ and let $q=-2d$. The good truncation $\tau_{\le q}C\to C$ is a quasi-isomorphism because cohomology above $q$ vanishes. The projection $\tau_{\le q}C\to L[-q]$ is a quasi-isomorphism because its kernel is acyclic (cohomology below $q$ vanishes and its degree-$q$ cycles equal its boundaries). These two quasi-isomorphisms give $\omega_f\cong L[2d]$. No local choices of a primitive root or of a basis of $L$ are glued into an orientation.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth, separated, compactifiable,
and of pure relative dimension $d$, with Noetherian base.
Put $\omega_f=f^\times A_S$, using the ambient right
adjoint. Then $\omega_f[-2d]$ is a locally constant
sheaf of free rank-one $A$-modules. For every complex
$K$ on $S$, the canonical tensor morphism is an
isomorphism

$$
f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}f^\times K.
$$

proof.text:
Construct the tensor morphism by transposing

$$
Rf_!(f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f)
\cong K\otimes_A^LRf_!\omega_f
\longrightarrow K\otimes_A^LA_S=K
$$

under [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint].
The displayed projection formula follows from
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] on a compactification:
extension by zero commutes with tensoring a pulled-back
complex, as its stalk is either that complex or zero.

By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], every point of
$X$ has an etale neighbourhood $u:U\to X$ such
that $fu=p_de$, where $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$
is etale (one may restrict the base to an open neighbourhood).
The adjunctions in
[lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction]
identify

$$
u^*f^\times K\cong e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d],\qquad
u^*\omega_f\cong A_U(d)[2d].
$$

By its definition as the transpose of the projection formula
and counit, the tensor map restricts under these identifications
to the canonical reassociation
$(fu)^*K\otimes_A^LA_U(d)[2d]\cong(fu)^*K(d)[2d]$.
To check this assertion, transpose on $U$: both maps
become the projection formula followed by the composite of
the etale counit with the $d$ affine-line counits. The
uniqueness in the adjunction bijection therefore identifies
them. In particular it is an isomorphism locally on $X$,
hence globally by
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative].

The same local calculation shows that all cohomology sheaves
of $\omega_f$ except $\mathcal H^{-2d}$ vanish,
and that $\mathcal H^{-2d}(\omega_f)$ is etale locally
free of rank one. The canonical truncation isomorphism
$\omega_f\cong\mathcal H^{-2d}(\omega_f)[2d]$
gives the stated conclusion. No complexes or morphisms were
glued in a derived category: the adjoint and tensor morphism
were constructed globally, and geometric stalks only tested
their properties.
